sections.history: Papanasam, whose historical temple name is Tiruppalaithurai, is an ancient Shaiva site on the southern bank of the Kaveri, hymned in the Tevaram and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The stone temple belongs to the Chola period with later additions, entered through a five-tiered gopuram. Within the complex stands a large brick granary of the Vijayanagara era, maintained as a protected monument — a reminder of the temple's role as a centre of the agrarian delta.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan, entered through a five-tiered gopuram, with the sanctum of Palaivananathar and the shrine of the goddess Dhavala Vennagai Ammai. The name of the lord recalls a forest of palai, the iron-wood tree, that once stood here. The notable brick granary within the precinct, of the Vijayanagara period, is cared for by the state archaeology department and sets the temple apart among the delta shrines.
sections.legends: The town's name, Papanasam — 'the destruction of sin' — comes from the tradition that Rama worshipped Shiva here to be freed of the sin incurred in slaying Ravana, making and consecrating lingams at the nearby Ramalingaswami temple. Another story tells of the sages of the Tharuka forest who sent a tiger against Shiva, which he subdued and wore as a skin. Rama, Lakshmana, Sita, the sage Gautama and Arjuna are all remembered among the lord's worshippers here, giving Papanasam a rich weave of puranic association.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi season and the annual Brahmotsavam. Its association with Rama and the washing-away of sin draws pilgrims seeking expiation, and the temple shares in the wider sanctity of the Papanasam region on the Kaveri.
sections.experience: Papanasam offers the pilgrim a temple whose very name promises release from sin — the place where Rama is said to have cleansed himself before the lord. The darshan of Palaivananathar, the towering gateway and the ancient granary give the visit the feel of a long-settled sacred centre at the heart of the delta.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Papanasam is a town in Thanjavur district, about 18 km from Kumbakonam and 30 km from Thanjavur; it has its own railway station and is well connected by bus.
